## Motivation

With everything from light-roast pour-overs to dark-roast cold brews on café menus, there’s plenty for coffee lovers to talk about. Ask a friend what kind of coffee they like, and they might answer without hesitation: “I always go for a dark roast.” But would a dark roast get their highest rating if they tasted four coffees without knowing which was which? That scenario motivates our main question: **Do we know what coffee we like?** Using the Coffee Survey, we will examine how closely respondents’ stated roast preferences align with their ratings of four coffee samples. We will also test whether respondents who rate their coffee expertise higher show greater agreement between what they say they prefer and what they rate most highly.

## Data source

We will use the [May 14, 2024 TidyTuesday Coffee Survey](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/tree/main/data/2024/2024-05-14).
The dataset includes respondents' coffee habits, stated preferences,
self-rated expertise, and tasting ratings for samples A through D.

## Planned analyses and visualizations

We will summarize brewing methods and stated roast preferences with
bar charts. We will compare the distributions of sample preference
ratings and explore whether rating patterns vary by expertise or
stated roast preference. Our main data-cleaning tasks will be
separating multiple-response survey fields, reshaping the tasting
ratings to one row per respondent per sample, and checking how many
respondents rated all four samples.

## Final products

We plan to produce a written report, a project website with selected
visualizations, and a short video summarizing our findings.
